influences.name: David Bowie
influences.context: Well, when we started talking about touring, I had just been reading about David Bowie's Station to Station tour. I'm not sure if this is entirely true, but as far as I can tell, he did actually go station to station. He didn't get on a plane. He even did the Trans-Siberian Railway.

influences.name: Jorge Luis Borges
influences.context: But what was the last heavy thing I read? Borges's Labyrinths. That was pretty cool. The idea is the story, you know. I tried reading it a few years ago, and I was like, 'What the fuck is this?' and then some guy in the pub explained to me what was going on and then I actually really enjoyed it.

influences.name: Modeselektor
influences.context: Because of the nature of the music software, within the music itself, the tendency is toward soft synths and soft effects—and I use these too—which are all internal, inside the computer. And I think that's making a big difference to music as well. Some of it's really exciting but some of it's a bit lame-ass. It gives everything a softness which is not very exciting to listen to. I know Modeselektor would love me for saying this.

influences.name: Karlheinz Stockhausen
influences.context: Thinking about it, digital albums could really be any length these days. You could make it five hours or you could do a Stockhausen thing and— What? With the helicopters? [Stockhausen's Helicopter String Quartet was written for string quartet and helicopter.] Yeah. He also wrote an opera that lasted seven days.

influences.name: Krzysztof Penderecki
influences.context: his longstanding love of Polish composer Krzysztof Penderecki, whose 'Threnody To The Victims Of Hiroshima' directly inspired Greenwood's award-winning 'Popcorn Superhet Receiver'

influences.name: Oliver Messiaen
influences.context: He regards French composer Oliver Messiaen as the greatest of all time – 'one of the few composers when you can hear just a few chords in isolation and know it's him'

influences.name: Steve Reich
influences.context: The next Octatonic release is likely to be a recording of work by another hero, Steve Reich.

influences.name: Bach
influences.context: Listening to Bach has the same feeling as when you're listening to Kraftwerk and you think 'electronic music doesn't get better than this'.

influences.name: Kraftwerk
influences.context: Listening to Bach has the same feeling as when you're listening to Kraftwerk and you think 'electronic music doesn't get better than this'.

influences.name: John Lennon
influences.context: And then there's that Lennon thing about it's not how you, what's it? ... It's not - yes - it's not who you steal from, it's how you steal.

influences.name: Nigel Godrich
influences.context: And to have the ability within our group with Nigel to sort of move around in all these different areas.

influences.name: John Lennon and Yoko Ono
influences.context: the poster sloganeering of OK Computer being inspired by John Lennon and Yoko Ono's "War Is Over!" billboard campaign. "Around that time I was totally obsessed with the Lennon thing," Yorke states.

influences.name: The Beatles
influences.context: a song from "OK Computer" inspired by the Beatles' "Sexy Sadie."

influences.name: Robert Rauschenberg
influences.context: As Robert Rauschenberg said (and quoted in the exhibition): "The artist's job is to be a witness to his time in history."
